body:
Sam (Acme): Hey team — running into intermittent 429s when we kick off a bulk embeddings job. We batch at 64 and run ~100 parallel workers. About 10-20% of requests return 429s with Retry-After and jobs fail fast. No obvious billing alerts on our side. Anyone seen similar burst throttling behavior?

Jessica (Support): Thanks for the report, Sam. Can you paste a short snippet of the failing request/response (headers + status) and confirm which model youre calling for embeddings? Also roughly how many vectors total & the time window.

Sam (Acme): Model: text-embedding-1536 (we thought it was the 1536 dims one). Total vectors: ~1.2M over ~30 minutes. Example response from our worker logs: 

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
Retry-After: 3
{ "error": "rate_limited", "message": "burst limit exceeded for embeddings.create" }
```

We also saw a handful of 400s earlier today: 

```
400 Bad Request {"error":"dimension_mismatch","expected_dim":1536,"received_dim":2048}
```

Not sure if that's related — could be a stray payload from a different model variant.

Marc (Infra): Large parallelism + small batches is the common pattern that hits rate and concurrency throttles. Two quick asks: 1) can you share your concurrency level per worker and 2) are you using our bulk/batched embeddings endpoint or issuing one-request-per-document?

Sam (Acme): We do one-request-per-batch (we build an array of 64 docs and call /v1/embeddings). Concurrency per worker: 100 workers across 8 hosts (~800 concurrent requests). We were trying to speed up throughput.

Jessica (Support): That's helpful. Root cause is likely cumulative request rate exceeding the account's embeddings per-minute quota + burst guardrails. The platform supports burst, but theres a soft per-account concurrency and minute window to protect stability. When burst exceeded, load shedding returns 429s with Retry-After.

Jessica (Support): Mitigations we recommend now: 
- Reduce concurrency (start with ~200 total concurrent requests)
- Increase batch size to 256 where feasible to reduce requests/sec
- Implement exponential backoff with jitter when you see 429, respect Retry-After header
- Consider using the bulk embeddings API (if not already) which handles internal batching more efficiently

Marc (Infra): Adding ops detail: we see a spike from your API key around 1805501200-1805501500 that hits 6k requests/min at peak. Your account tier quota is 3k r/min and a burst window of ~5k. The spike crossed the burst threshold, so throttling triggered. Linking internal metric chart: https://internal.redwood/metrics/keys/ACME-123 (ops-only)

Sam (Acme): OK makes sense. Is there a recommended backoff strategy? We're currently doing linear retry up to 3 attempts.

Jessica (Support): Use exponential backoff with full jitter. Example pseudo: 

```
base = 0.5s
retry = base * 2**attempt
delay = random_between(0, retry)
max_attempts = 8
```

Also obey Retry-After when present and treat 429 as retriable but throttle-aware — dont immediately spin more requests.

Sam (Acme): Noted. Any quick win to avoid having to re-run the whole job? Were half done and re-running 1.2M vectors is expensive.

Jessica (Support): Two immediate options: 
1) Add a local coordinator to cap concurrency and gradually drain remaining queue (preferred).
2) Request a temporary quota bump from Support/Billing for this specific run. I can open a bill/ops escalation now if you want — it may take a few hours. Which do you prefer?

Sam (Acme): Could you open the escalation? We'd like minimal reruns while we throttle back concurrency.

Jessica (Support): Done — opened INC-5721 for a temporary quota increase and flagged Billing. ETA for review ~3h. Tagging @billing-bot to speed approval.

billing-bot: Billing note: we need formal approval from finance for >100% quota temporary increases. Please confirm expected run cost and duration.

Sam (Acme): Estimated extra cost: ~$260 for the 1.2M vectors if we finish in the next 2 hours. Happy to provide a card on file.

Jessica (Support): Shared that with billing. Meanwhile, to prevent the earlier 400 dimension errors: verify every worker uses the same model and verify vector length before sending. Simple sanity check: 

```
if len(vector) != 1536:
  log.error("bad-dim", len(vector))
  drop/convert
```

Sam (Acme): We have a stray legacy process that was queuing vectors at 2048 — fixing that now. Good catch.

Marc (Infra): Long-term suggestions from infra: 
- Move to larger batch sizes and fewer concurrent clients
- Use the SDKs built-in batching helper (it merges small docs into fewer requests)
- If embeddings are throughput-critical, consider Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) or a scheduled window for large jobs. Those remove soft burst limits.

Jessica (Support): Ill follow up once billing confirms the temporary bump. Also created a small KB we can share internally for customers doing large bulk embeddings: https://redwood.help/embeddings/bulk-best-practices

Sam (Acme): Thanks team — we'll cap concurrency to 200, switch to 256 batch size where memory allows, add jittered backoff, and finish the remaining queue while you try the quota bump. Appreciate the quick triage. :thumbsup:

Marc (Infra): Well also check whether the burst thresholds should be tuned for this account if they plan recurring large runs. Filed ENG-9482 to review burst policy for high-volume customers.

Jessica (Support): Closing the loop after billing. Will update thread when quota bump is approved or if infra finds anything abnormal.

ops-bot: Incident INC-5721 created and assigned to billing.

Sam (Acme): will monitor and report back if we still hit 429s after throttling. Thanks all.
